Two-Time PDC Challenge Tour Winner (2023): Claimed secondary-tour crowns at Events 4 and 18 before graduating to full-time Tour Card status via 2025 Q-School.
Grand Slam of Darts Qualifier (2025 & 2026): Competed in consecutive group stages in Wolverhampton following his youth circuit dominance.
2026 PDC World Championship Debut: Made his maiden appearance at Alexandra Palace after climbing inside the world's top 70.
quote: Getting my Tour Card changed everything—now it's about proving week in, week out on the ProTour that I belong against the best.
fun_fact: Crabtree is an avid Arsenal supporter, travels to PDC events with close friend and fellow Tour Card holder Owen Bates, and has a younger brother, Cody, who also competes on the PDC Development Tour.
bio: Cam Crabtree is an English professional darts player who rose through the youth and secondary circuits—winning two Challenge Tour and six Development Tour titles—before earning his PDC Tour Card at 2025 Q-School. He has since reached multiple senior Players Championship semi-finals and qualified for the Grand Slam of Darts and World Championship.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Cam Crabtree — Shazam. Six-time Development Tour champion and rising English star lighting up the PDC ProTour. #DartsDaily

name: Wesley Plaisier
highlights: Players Championship 28 Winner (2024): Became only the fourth player in PDC history to win a senior ranking title without holding a Tour Card, beating Josh Rock 8–7 in the final.
Two-Time WDF World Masters Champion (2022 & 2024): Dominated the WDF major circuit by capturing two World Masters titles alongside two Belgium Open crowns.
Four-Time PDC Challenge Tour Champion: Won four Challenge Tour events between 2022 and 2024 to earn his maiden PDC Tour Card for 2025–2026.
PDC World Championship Last 32 (2026): Reached the third round at Alexandra Palace, pushing Krzysztof Ratajski to a seven-set thriller (4–3).
ProTour Nine-Darter (2026): Struck a nine-dart finish against Damon Heta at Players Championship 32 in Den Bosch.
quote: Winning a Players Championship without a Tour Card gave me the belief that my game stacks up against anyone in the PDC.
fun_fact: Before winning his first PDC Tour Card in 2025, Plaisier represented the Netherlands at the 2023 WDF World Cup in Esbjerg, winning gold in both the men's team and overall categories.
bio: Wesley Plaisier is a Dutch professional darts player and two-time WDF World Masters champion who made history in 2024 by winning Players Championship 28 without a Tour Card. After securing full-time PDC status via the Challenge Tour rankings, he reached the last 32 of the 2026 PDC World Championship.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Wesley Plaisier — Two-time World Masters winner who captured a PDC ranking title before even holding a Tour Card. #DartsDaily

name: Adam Lipscombe
highlights: Maiden PDC Ranking Finalist (2025): Reached the final of Players Championship 7 in his debut Tour Card season before falling 8–3 to Gary Anderson.
2025 Players Championship Finals Last 16: Made a deep televised major run in Minehead, missing 10 match darts in a deciding-leg thriller against Daryl Gurney.
First PDC Tour Card (2025): Earned full-time professional status via 2025 UK Q-School after finishing runner-up at the 2024 ADC Global Championship.
Back-to-Back UK Open Last 64 Runs (2025 & 2026): Reached the fourth round in consecutive appearances at Butlin's Minehead Resort.
2026 PDC World Championship Qualifier: Qualified for his maiden Alexandra Palace campaign after breaking into the world's top 80.
quote: Getting my Tour Card turned my life around—it gave me the platform to test myself against the world's best every week.
fun_fact: Outside of competing on the PDC circuit, Lipscombe worked full-time as a groundworker before capturing his Tour Card at 2025 Q-School.
bio: Adam Lipscombe is an English darts player who transitioned from the amateur circuit to secure a PDC Tour Card at 2025 UK Q-School. In his rookie professional season, he reached his first Players Championship final, advanced to the last 16 of the Players Championship Finals, and qualified for the 2026 PDC World Championship.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Adam Lipscombe — Baby Boy. Former groundworker turned PDC ProTour finalist making waves on the big stage. #DartsDaily

name: Cor Dekker
highlights: First Norwegian PDC Tour Card Winner (2025): Topped the 2025 European Q-School Order of Merit to become the first player representing Norway to earn a PDC Tour Card.
2025 Swiss Darts Trophy Semi-Finalist: Reached his maiden PDC European Tour semi-final in Basel during his first full season on the ProTour.
Three-Time PDC Nordic & Baltic Pro Tour Champion: Claimed regional ranking titles in 2018 and twice in 2026.
European Tour Nine-Darter (2024): Struck a live-streamed nine-dart finish at the 2024 Hungarian Darts Trophy, matching Michael van Gerwen's nine-darter in the same tournament.
Multiple PDC World Cup of Darts Appearances: Represented Norway on the international stage across multiple World Cup campaigns, reaching the last 16 in 2016 and 2026.
quote: "It must be something with the Scandinavian girls!" (joking about the wave of Dutch-born players moving to the Nordic and Baltic regions)
fun_fact: Born in Bovenkarspel in the Netherlands, Dekker relocated to Askim, Norway, and became the first Norwegian representative in history to win a PDC Tour Card at Q-School.
bio: Cor Dekker is a Dutch-born Norwegian professional darts player who made history in January 2025 as the first representative of Norway to win a PDC Tour Card. A three-time winner on the PDC Nordic & Baltic Tour, he reached his first European Tour semi-final in 2025 and competed at the 2026 PDC World Championship.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Cor Dekker — The Sheriff. Norway's first-ever PDC Tour Card holder and European Tour semi-finalist. #DartsDaily

name: Dominik Gruellich
highlights: Maiden PDC Ranking Finalist (2025): Reached the final of Players Championship 14 after defeating Daryl Gurney, Dirk van Duijvenbode, and Michael Smith before losing to Jonny Clayton.
Two-Time PDC Development Tour Champion (2025): Won Development Tour Events 10 and 21 during a breakout 2025 campaign.
2026 UK Open Last 32: Advanced to the fifth round of the televised major in Minehead for his deepest major run to date.
2026 PDC World Championship Debut: Qualified for his first Alexandra Palace appearance, pushing Jermaine Wattimena to a final-set decider (3–2).
First PDC Tour Card (2025): Earned a two-year Tour Card at European Q-School in Kalkar after coming back from 2–0 down to beat Rusty-Jake Rodriguez 6–3 in his decisive match.
quote: I was in the tunnel and just tried to get the best possible result because every leg really counts at Q-School.
fun_fact: Grüllich works as a landscape gardener in Bavaria with the full backing of his employer, and he successfully overcame an early-career bout of dartitis before winning his PDC Tour Card.
bio: Dominik Grüllich is a German professional darts player who overcame early-career dartitis to win two PDC Development Tour titles and earn his Tour Card at 2025 European Q-School. During his debut ProTour season, he reached his first Players Championship final and qualified for the 2026 PDC World Championship.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Dominik Grüllich — Bavarian landscape gardener turned PDC ProTour finalist and rising star of German darts. #DartsDaily

name: Andy Boulton
highlights: Four-Time PDC Challenge Tour Champion: Won two titles in 2023 (CT 3 and 23) and swept both events on 16 March 2024 (CT 8 and 9) in a single day.
2025 UK Q-School Comeback: Regained his PDC Tour Card by finishing eighth on the 2025 UK Q-School Order of Merit.
2011 UK Open Last 16: Produced his deepest televised PDC major run by reaching the fifth round in Bolton.
Multiple BDO & PDC World Championship Appearances: Competed across both codes at Lakeside (reaching the Last 16 in 2008) and Alexandra Palace (reaching Round 2 in 2021).
2011 Scottish National Champion: Captured the national singles crown alongside titles at the Granite City Open and North Lanarkshire Open.
quote: Winning two Challenge Tour titles in a single day proved to me that the scoring power is still right there.
fun_fact: Born in Stoke-on-Trent, Boulton moved to Ardrossan in North Ayrshire, Scotland, and switched his sporting allegiance to represent Scotland on the international stage.
bio: Andy Boulton is a veteran Scottish darts player who has competed at both the BDO and PDC World Championships across a career spanning more than two decades. After capturing four PDC Challenge Tour titles across 2023 and 2024, he reclaimed his full-time PDC Tour Card at 2025 UK Q-School.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Andy Boulton — X-Factor. Four-time Challenge Tour champion and seasoned World Championship competitor back on the PDC ProTour. #DartsDaily

name: Jim Long
walk_on_music: Inner Circle - Sweat (A La La La La Long)
highlights: First PDC Tour Card at Age 56 (2025): Won his maiden PDC Tour Card outright at 2025 UK Q-School, becoming one of the oldest Q-School graduates in history.
Six-Time CDC Pro Tour Champion: Dominated the North American Championship Darts Corporation circuit with six ranking titles between 2019 and 2025.
2024 World Seniors Darts Championship Semi-Finalist: Defeated David Cameron, Martin Adams, and Paul Hogan to reach the last four at Circus Tavern.
2023 US Darts Masters Giant-Killing: Shocked reigning world champion Michael Smith at Madison Square Garden on the World Series of Darts stage.
2019 PDC World Championship Round 2 & World Cup Quarter-Finalist: Beat Mickey Mansell on his Alexandra Palace debut and helped Canada reach the 2019 World Cup quarter-finals.
quote: Age is just a number if you still have the hunger to compete and put the work in on the practice board.
fun_fact: Long didn't start playing darts until he was 19 years old, yet he went on to win his first-ever PDC Tour Card at age 56 and memorably knocked out then-World Champion Michael Smith at Madison Square Garden in 2023.
bio: Jim Long is a veteran Canadian darts player and six-time CDC Pro Tour champion who stunned the sport by winning his first PDC Tour Card at 2025 Q-School at age 56. He has represented Canada at multiple PDC World Cups and reached the semi-finals of the 2024 World Seniors Darts Championship.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Jim Long — The Gentleman. Canada's six-time CDC Pro Tour champion who proved age is just a number by winning a PDC Tour Card at 56. #DartsDaily

name: Oskar Lukasiak
highlights: First PDC Tour Card (2025): Finished fourth on the 2025 European Q-School Order of Merit to earn full-time professional status.
Two-Time PDC World Cup of Darts Quarter-Finalist: Guided Sweden to back-to-back quarter-final appearances in 2023 (with Dennis Nilsson) and 2024 (with Jeffrey de Graaf).
PDC Challenge Tour 3 Winner (2024): Captured his maiden PDC secondary-tour title by beating Danny Jansen 5–3 in the final.
Three-Time PDC Nordic & Baltic Tour Champion: Won regional ranking events across 2024, 2025, and 2026.
2026 PDC World Championship Debut: Qualified for his first Alexandra Palace appearance after climbing inside the world's top 90.
quote: Representing Sweden in the World Cup quarter-finals showed what Scandinavian darts can achieve on the biggest stages.
fun_fact: At the 2004 Denmark Open, Lukasiak hit a nine-dart finish during a boys' match at just 12 years old—making him the youngest player in history at the time to record an official competitive nine-darter.
bio: Oskar Lukasiak is a Swedish professional darts player who gained early fame by hitting a competitive nine-darter at age 12 and winning the 2004 World Masters Boys title. After helping Sweden reach consecutive PDC World Cup quarter-finals and winning on the Challenge Tour, he secured his PDC Tour Card at 2025 Q-School.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Oskar Lukasiak — Former child prodigy who hit a nine-darter at 12 and led Sweden to back-to-back World Cup quarter-finals. #DartsDaily

name: Jimmy van Schie
highlights: 2025 WDF World Champion: Rallied from 3–0 down in sets to defeat Mitchell Lawrie 6–3 in the Lakeside final to capture his first world crown.
2025 WDF World Masters Champion: Defeated Jeff Smith 7–2 in the final to become just the fourth Dutchman to lift the historic title.
Former WDF World No. 1 & 14-Time Ranking Winner: Dominated the WDF circuit across 2024–2025, winning eight ranking titles in 2024 alone to top the world rankings.
PDC Challenge Tour 18 Champion (2024): Captured his maiden PDC secondary-tour title by edging Daniel Ayres 5–4.
2026 PDC Tour Card Winner: Secured full-time PDC ProTour status at European Q-School in January 2026 immediately after his Lakeside triumph.
quote: This feels amazing. Lakeside is special — the crowd, the stage, everything. I'm enjoying it, but I also know: the work isn't finished yet.
fun_fact: Standing 6 feet 9 inches (2.07 m) tall, Van Schie is one of the tallest players in professional darts—earning him the nickname "The Dutch Sequoia"—and he completed the rare WDF World Masters and World Championship double in late 2025 before winning his PDC Tour Card weeks later.
bio: Jimmy van Schie is a towering Dutch darts player who dominated the WDF circuit as world number one, capturing both the 2025 World Masters and 2025 WDF World Championship. Immediately following his Lakeside triumph, he transitioned full-time to the PDC by securing a Tour Card at 2026 Q-School.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Jimmy van Schie — The Dutch Sequoia. 2025 WDF World Champion and World Masters winner bringing towering power to the PDC Tour. #DartsDaily

name: Thomas Lovely
highlights: First PDC Tour Card on Sixth Attempt (2025): Showed remarkable persistence at 2025 UK Q-School to secure his maiden two-year Tour Card on his sixth Q-School appearance.
2025 UK Open Last 64: Won three matches at Butlin's Minehead Resort to reach the fourth round of the televised major before falling to Rob Cross.
Multiple PDC European Tour Appearances: Qualified for stage events in Germany and Belgium during his debut season as a Tour Card holder.
PDC Development Tour Quarter-Finalist & World Youth Qualifier: Reached the last 16 of the 2018 PDC World Youth Championship and competed on the Development Tour earlier in his career.
Rileys Amateur Qualifier (2024): Earned his televised PDC major debut at the 2024 UK Open via the grassroots pub qualifying route.
quote: Six years of going back to Q-School teaches you resilience—finally getting over the line for a Tour Card made every setback worth it.
fun_fact: ovely qualified for his televised major debut at the 2024 UK Open through a grassroots Rileys pub qualifier and finally earned his PDC Tour Card in 2025 on his sixth trip to Q-School.
bio: Thomas Lovely is an English professional darts player who rose from Rileys pub qualifiers and the PDC Development Tour to earn his first Tour Card at 2025 UK Q-School on his sixth attempt. He went on to reach the last 64 of the 2025 UK Open and establish himself on the PDC ProTour.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Thomas Lovely — Six-time Q-School grinder whose persistence paid off with a PDC Tour Card and UK Open breakthrough. #DartsDaily

name: Leon Weber
highlights: First PDC Tour Card (2025): Earned a two-year Tour Card via the 2025 European Q-School Order of Merit after reaching the Day 1 quarter-finals in Kalkar.
European Darts Grand Prix Debut Win (2025): Defeated Ryan Joyce 6–3 in Sindelfingen with 112 and 156 finishes on his maiden European Tour stage appearance.
ProTour Nine-Darter (2025): Struck a live-streamed nine-dart finish during a Players Championship event in Leicester.
Players Championship Quarter-Finalist (2026): Reached the last eight at Players Championship 8 in March 2026 to climb inside the world's top 95.
2026 UK Open & Players Championship Finals Qualifier: Reached the last 64 at the 2026 UK Open and qualified for the season-ending finals in Minehead.
quote: "No one can ever take that experience away from me. It's an amazing feeling to have it on video too. I've watched it an incredible number of times to this day." (reflecting on his Leicester ProTour nine-darter)
fun_fact: Although he does not use an official stage nickname, Weber joked during a 2026 live stream that "Leon – The Professional"—after the 1994 cult classic film—would be his top choice.
bio: Leon Weber is a German professional darts player who earned his first PDC Tour Card at 2025 European Q-School. Since joining the full-time circuit, he has recorded a ProTour nine-dart finish, reached a Players Championship quarter-final, and broken into the world's top 95.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Leon Weber — German ProTour nine-dart hero making steady strides up the PDC Order of Merit. #DartsDaily

name: Viktor Tingstrom
highlights: Outright European Q-School Day 1 Winner (2025): Defeated Jimmy van Schie 6–4 in the opening final at Kalkar to become the first player to win a Tour Card at 2025 Q-School.
2023 Finnish Masters Champion: Captured his maiden WDF ranking title by defeating Brian Løkken in the final.
2023 PDC World Youth Championship Giant-Killing: Knocked out top seed Adam Gawlas in the group stage before reaching the last 16.
PDC Nordic & Baltic ProTour Finalist (2026): Reached the final of Nordic & Baltic ProTour 12 in 2026 alongside multiple European Tour appearances.
WDF Europe & World Cup Youth Representative: Represented Sweden internationally from age 11, including the 2024 WDF Europe Cup.
quote: Winning on Day 1 at Q-School was a dream start—it gave me two full years to test myself against the world's best.
fun_fact: Tingström began representing Sweden at WDF youth international tournaments at just 11 years old before winning his PDC Tour Card outright on the very first day of 2025 European Q-School.
bio: Viktor Tingström is a Swedish professional darts player and former Finnish Masters champion who captured his first PDC Tour Card outright on Day 1 of 2025 European Q-School. A longtime Swedish youth international, he has since competed on the PDC ProTour, European Tour, and Nordic & Baltic circuit.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Viktor Tingström — Headhunter. Sweden's Day 1 Q-School winner bringing Scandinavian firepower to the PDC Tour. #DartsDaily

name: Shane McGuirk
highlights: 2024 WDF World Champion: Became the first player from the Republic of Ireland to win a senior darts world championship, dropping just three sets all tournament and beating Paul Lim 6–3 in the final.
First PDC Tour Card (2026): Secured full-time PDC status at 2026 UK Q-School after missing out by a single point in 2021.
119.29 Challenge Tour Average (2024): Posted a blistering 119.29 three-dart average in a 5–0 whitewash over Stefaan Henderyck at Challenge Tour 21.
2019 PDC Development Tour 13 Champion: Defeated Keane Barry 5–4 in the final to claim his first PDC youth title.
2023 WDF Irish Open & 2022 FCD Anniversary Open Champion: Won back-to-back WDF ranking crowns, including a 5–4 final victory over Andy Baetens.
quote: Becoming the first world champion from the Republic of Ireland is something nobody can ever take away—now it's about carrying that belief onto the PDC Tour.
fun_fact: Before committing full-time to darts, McGuirk played Gaelic football at underage level for Aughnamullen GAA in County Monaghan, and he did not drop a single set at the 2024 WDF World Championship until the final against Paul Lim.
bio: Shane McGuirk is an Irish professional darts player who made history in 2024 as the first competitor from the Republic of Ireland to win a senior world title at the WDF World Championship. After recording a 119.29 average on the Challenge Tour, he secured his maiden PDC Tour Card at 2026 Q-School.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Shane McGuirk — The Arrow. The Republic of Ireland's first senior World Darts Champion now firing on the PDC ProTour. #DartsDaily

name: Marvin van Velzen
walk_on_music: 2 Brothers on the 4th Floor - Come Take My Hand
highlights: MODUS Super Series Season 8 Champion (2024): Won a weekly title in August 2024 and returned weeks later to capture the entire Season 8 Champions Week crown.
Televised MODUS Super Series Nine-Darter (2024): Fired a live nine-dart leg on 8 August 2024 during his title-winning campaign.
First PDC Tour Card (2025): Earned a two-year Tour Card via 2025 European Q-School in Kalkar.
Double WDF Europe Cup Youth Gold Medalist (2017): Captured both the boys' team and overall gold medals representing the Netherlands.
2024 Inaugural Benelux Open Champion: Defeated Bradley Roes in the final to qualify for the 2024 ADC Global Championship quarter-finals.
quote: Winning the MODUS Super Series Champions Week proved I can handle pressure under the TV lights and beat anyone on my day.
fun_fact: Van Velzen won a weekly MODUS Super Series title, hit a televised nine-darter, and captured the overall Season 8 Champions Week trophy all within the same month of August 2024.
bio: Marvin van Velzen is a Dutch professional darts player and former WDF Europe Cup Youth double gold medalist who surged onto the PDC circuit by winning MODUS Super Series Season 8 in 2024. He secured his first PDC Tour Card at 2025 European Q-School and has since competed regularly on the ProTour.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Marvin van Velzen — The Terminator. MODUS Super Series Season 8 champion and televised nine-dart hero on the PDC Tour. #DartsDaily

name: Owen Bates
highlights: Three-Time PDC Development Tour Winner: Captured two titles in 2025 and added a third in 2026 to finish third on the 2025 Development Tour rankings.
Two-Time PDC World Championship Qualifier (2024 & 2026): Reached Alexandra Palace via the 2023 Challenge Tour and returned in 2026 through his youth circuit dominance.
2023 PDC Challenge Tour Winner: Claimed his maiden secondary-tour title in August 2023 to clinch his first PDC Tour Card.
MODUS Super Series Weekly Champion (2023): Defeated Leonard Gates 4–3 in a deciding-leg final to pocket the £5,000 top prize.
Back-to-Back UK Open Last 128 Runs (2024 & 2025): Competed in consecutive televised UK Open campaigns in Minehead.
quote: Having to drop my old nickname gave me plenty of headlines before my Ally Pally debut, but I want my darts on the board to do the talking.
fun_fact: Ahead of his PDC World Championship debut at Alexandra Palace in December 2023, Bates made international sports headlines when the Darts Regulation Authority banned him from walking on with his cheeky teenage nickname, "The Master".
bio: Owen Bates is an English professional darts player who earned his initial PDC Tour Card through the 2023 Challenge Tour before winning three PDC Development Tour titles across 2025 and 2026. He has qualified for two PDC World Championships and climbed inside the world's top 85.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Owen Bates — Three-time Development Tour champion and two-time World Championship qualifier rising out of Devon. #DartsDaily

name: Tavis Dudeney
highlights: First PDC Tour Card (2025): Secured a two-year Tour Card at 2025 UK Q-School by defeating Martijn Dragt 7–4 in his qualifying final.
2024 PDC Development Tour 23 Champion: Claimed his maiden PDC youth ranking title by defeating Jurjen van der Velde in the final.
2026 PDC World Championship Debut: Qualified for his first Alexandra Palace appearance via the Tour Card Holder Qualifier in November 2025.
2024 British International Men's Champion: Represented England's senior men's team to capture the team title alongside semi-final runs at the British Open and British Classic.
2021 JDC Advanced Tour Event 9 Winner: Won on the Junior Darts Corporation circuit at age 17 after starting local league darts at age seven.
quote: Coming from behind in that Q-School final to win my Tour Card was the biggest moment of my career—everything I've worked toward since I was seven.
fun_fact: Dudeney began playing competitive local league darts at just seven years old, and he rallied from an early deficit to beat Martijn Dragt 7–4 at 2025 Q-School to turn full-time professional.
bio: Tavis Dudeney is an English professional darts player and former Development Tour event winner who secured his PDC Tour Card at 2025 UK Q-School. He capped his rookie ProTour campaign by qualifying for the 2026 PDC World Championship and breaking into the world's top 100.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Tavis Dudeney — The Dude. Former Development Tour champion who fought his way through Q-School onto the PDC World Championship stage. #DartsDaily

name: Adam Gawlas
walk_on_music: Delinquent Habits - Return of the Tres
highlights: 2023 UK Open Semi-Finalist: Became the first Czech player in history to reach a televised PDC major semi-final, losing narrowly to eventual champion Andrew Gilding.
2019 PDC World Youth Championship Runner-Up: Reached the final at Minehead at age 17, falling 6–0 to Luke Humphries.
Two-Time PDC Development Tour Champion (2023 & 2026): Captured youth ranking titles three years apart to underline his pedigree.
Two-Time PDC World Championship Qualifier (2023 & 2026): Reached the second round on debut in 2023 and returned to Alexandra Palace in 2026.
2026 PDC Q-School Comeback: After losing his Tour Card in January 2025, he regained full-time status at European Q-School in January 2026.
quote: Reaching the UK Open semi-finals proved that Czech darts can compete right at the very top of the PDC.
fun_fact: Gawlas first picked up a set of darts at age 16 after a serious knee injury ended his promising youth ice hockey career—and within 18 months he was playing in the PDC World Youth Championship final.
bio: Adam Gawlas is a trailblazing Czech professional darts player who became the first player from his country to reach a televised PDC major semi-final at the 2023 UK Open. After briefly losing his Tour Card at the end of 2024, he reclaimed full-time status at 2026 Q-School and won his second Development Tour title.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Adam Gawlas — Flawlas. Czech darts' first televised PDC major semi-finalist back on the ProTour. #DartsDaily

name: Jurjen van der Velde
highlights: Ten-Time PDC Secondary Tour Winner: Captured seven PDC Development Tour titles and three PDC Challenge Tour titles across his career.
2024 PDC World Youth Championship Runner-Up: Narrowly missed five match darts in a dramatic 6–5 final defeat to compatriot Gian van Veen.
2025 Grand Slam of Darts Last 16 & UK Open Last 32: Reached the knockout stages in Wolverhampton and knocked out Bradley Brooks and Keane Barry in Minehead.
2018 JDC World Champion & BDO World Youth Masters Winner: Swept both major youth world titles at age 15 alongside multiple WDF Europe and World Cup youth golds.
2026 PDC Tour Card Comeback & World Championship Debut: Made his Alexandra Palace debut in 2026 and regained his Tour Card for the 2026–2027 seasons.
quote: Missing five match darts in the World Youth final hurt badly, but it made me hungrier to come back stronger on the big stages.
fun_fact: At just 15 years old in 2018, Van der Velde pulled off a historic youth double by winning both the JDC World Darts Championship and the BDO World Youth Masters in the same year.
bio: Jurjen van der Velde is a decorated Dutch darts talent who won both the JDC World Championship and World Youth Masters at age 15 before capturing ten combined titles across the PDC Development and Challenge Tours. Following a runner-up finish at the 2024 World Youth Championship and a Grand Slam knockout run, he reclaimed his PDC Tour Card for 2026.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Jurjen van der Velde — JVV. Ten-time PDC secondary-tour winner and former youth world champion lighting up the ProTour. #DartsDaily

name: Greg Ritchie
highlights: First PDC Tour Card (2025): Secured full-time professional status at 2025 UK Q-School after nearly a decade competing on the Development and Challenge Tours.
2026 UK Open Last 64: Produced his best televised PDC major run in Minehead by reaching the fourth round after also making the third round in 2025.
Players Championship Last 16 (2025): Reached his maiden senior PDC ProTour last 16 at Players Championship 8 in Hildesheim in March 2025.
Three-Time PDC Development Tour Finalist (2019): Reached three youth ranking finals in a single season to qualify for his UK Open debut in 2020.
WDF World Masters Last 32 (2022): Advanced to the fourth round of the historic WDF major before winning his PDC Tour Card.
quote: After years of grinding on the Challenge Tour and coming close at Q-School, finally earning my Tour Card is the reward for never giving up.
fun_fact: Ritchie spent nearly nine years competing across the PDC Development Tour, Challenge Tour, and Q-School—including losing three Development Tour finals in 2019—before finally breaking through to win his Tour Card in 2025.
bio: Greg Ritchie is a Scottish professional darts player whose persistence across nearly a decade on the PDC secondary circuits paid off when he earned his Tour Card at 2025 UK Q-School. He has since reached the last 16 on the Players Championship circuit and advanced to the last 64 of the 2026 UK Open.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Greg Ritchie — Musselburgh's persistent Scottish grinder who turned years of Challenge Tour graft into a PDC Tour Card. #DartsDaily

name: Jeffrey De Zwaan
walk_on_music: Major Lazer - Watch Out For This
highlights: 2018 World Matchplay Semi-Finalist: Shocked world number one Michael van Gerwen 10–6 in the first round as world number 68 before reaching the semi-finals in Blackpool.
Two-Time PDC Players Championship Winner: Captured senior ranking titles at PC 10 in 2018 (beating Jonny Clayton 6–5) and PC 14 in 2019 (beating Stephen Bunting 8–2).

2020 PDC World Championship Last 16 & World Grand Prix Quarter-Finalist: Reached the fourth round at Alexandra Palace—pushing eventual champion Peter Wright to a 4–3 thriller—and made the last eight in Dublin.
Premier League Darts Contender (2019 & 2020): Selected twice as a guest contender in Rotterdam, defeating Rob Cross in front of his home crowd in 2019.
2026 PDC Q-School Comeback: Reclaimed his PDC Tour Card at European Q-School in January 2026 after overcoming recurring shoulder injuries that had sidelined him from the top 64.
quote: Beating Michael van Gerwen on the World Matchplay stage changed my career—now that my shoulder is healthy, I know what level I can reach again.
fun_fact: In 2018, De Zwaan defeated world number one Michael van Gerwen at both the UK Open—snapping Van Gerwen's nearly four-year unbeaten streak in ITV majors—and the World Matchplay despite entering Blackpool ranked 68th in the world.
bio: Jeffrey de Zwaan is a two-time PDC Players Championship winner and 2018 World Matchplay semi-finalist renowned for toppling Michael van Gerwen in multiple televised majors. After battling through persistent shoulder injuries that cost him his Tour Card at the end of 2024, he reclaimed full-time status at 2026 Q-School.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Jeffrey de Zwaan — The Black Cobra. Two-time ProTour champion and 2018 World Matchplay semi-finalist striking back on the PDC circuit. #DartsDaily

name: Kai Gotthardt
walk_on_music: Dynoro & Gigi D'Agostino - In My Mind
highlights: 2024 PDC Europe Super League Champion: Defeated Paul Krohne 8–5 in the final to qualify for his maiden PDC World Championship.

highlights: First PDC Tour Card at Age 51 (2025): Earned a two-year Tour Card at 2025 European Q-School in Kalkar to join Belgium's growing PDC contingent.
Multiple PDC European Tour Appearances: Qualified for stage events in Belgium and Germany during his career on the PDC circuit.
Back-to-Back UK Open Appearances (2025 & 2026): Competed in consecutive televised UK Open campaigns in Minehead as a Tour Card holder.
PDC Challenge Tour Regular & Finalist: Built his credentials on the Challenge Tour circuit prior to graduating to full-time ProTour status.
Signature One80 Equipment Range: Collaborated with One80 to release his own signature 90% tungsten darts.
quote: Winning my Tour Card at 51 proves that if you keep working hard and believing in your game, it is never too late.
fun_fact: Henderyck secured his first-ever PDC Tour Card at 2025 European Q-School just days after turning 51 years old, making him one of the oldest rookie Tour Card holders in European Q-School history.
bio: Stefaan Henderyck is a Belgian professional darts player who defied age by winning his first PDC Tour Card at 2025 European Q-School at age 51. He has since competed in consecutive UK Opens and multiple European Tour events on the PDC circuit.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Stefaan Henderyck — Belgium's persistent 51-year-old Q-School graduate proving it's never too late on the PDC Tour. #DartsDaily

name: Tytus Kanik
highlights: First Polish PDC Tour Card Holder (2018): Made national history at 2018 European Q-School by becoming the first player from Poland to win a PDC Tour Card.
2019 Austrian Darts Open Last 16: Defeated Steve Lennon and Mensur Suljović on the European Tour stage before narrowly losing 6–5 to Peter Wright.
Two-Time Polish National Champion (2017 & 2022): Captured two national singles crowns, defeating Sebastian Białecki 5–3 in the 2022 final.
Four-Time PDC World Cup of Darts Representative: Represented Poland alongside Krzysztof Ratajski from 2015 to 2019, reaching the second round in 2019.
2025 PDC Tour Card Comeback: Regained his full-time PDC Tour Card at 2025 European Q-School after a five-year spell away from the main tour.
quote: Becoming the first Polish player with a PDC Tour Card opened the door for Polish darts—winning it back in 2025 felt just as special.
fun_fact: Before switching to darts, Kanik was an accomplished competitive pool player who won a bronze medal at the 2003 Polish Eight-Ball Billiards Championships—and he also won three EDF European soft-tip gold medals.
bio: Tytus Kanik is a pioneering Polish professional darts player and former national pool medalist who became the first player from Poland to earn a PDC Tour Card in 2018. A two-time Polish Champion and four-time World Cup representative, he reclaimed full-time PDC status at 2025 Q-School.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Tytus Kanik — Tito. Poland's first-ever PDC Tour Card holder and two-time national champion back on the ProTour. #DartsDaily

name: Samuel Price
highlights: Outright UK Q-School Day 4 Winner (2026): Won the final event of 2026 UK Q-School—averaging 102.13 along the way—to clinch his maiden PDC Tour Card.
Multiple 2026 PDC European Tour Qualifiers: Won Tour Card Holder Qualifiers for both the 2026 European Darts Open and 2026 Hungarian Darts Trophy.
2026 UK Open Debut: Made his first televised PDC major appearance in Minehead during his rookie season on the tour.
Top-100 PDC European Tour Ranking: Climbed inside the top 95 on the PDC European Tour Order of Merit in his debut card-holding year.
Former Challenge Tour Contender: Progressed through the PDC Challenge Tour before breaking through at Q-School at age 32.
quote: Winning on the final day of Q-School when everything is on the line is the ultimate test of nerve.
fun_fact: Price held his nerve on the dramatic final day of 2026 UK Q-School to win the Day 4 tournament outright, immediately qualifying for multiple European Tour events in his rookie year.
bio: Samuel Price is an English professional darts player who captured his first PDC Tour Card outright on the final day of 2026 UK Q-School. In his debut full-time campaign, he debuted at the UK Open and qualified for multiple PDC European Tour stage events.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Samuel Price — Pricey. Coventry's final-day UK Q-School winner making his mark on the PDC European Tour. #DartsDaily

name: Yorick Hofkens
walk_on_music: Ini Kamoze - Here Comes the Hotstepper
highlights: PDC Development Tour 19 Champion (2026): Defeated Adam Gawlas 5–4 in Hildesheim to capture his maiden PDC youth ranking crown.
Outright European Q-School Day 3 Winner (2026): Won his first PDC Tour Card at age 18 by winning the Day 3 final at 2026 European Q-School.
2023 WDF Europe Cup Youth Singles Gold Medalist: Won the prestigious European boys' singles title representing Germany at age 16.
2026 UK Open Debut: Made his televised PDC major debut in Minehead at age 18, posting a 93.45 average against Owen Bates.
2025 Baltic Sea Darts Open Qualifier: Qualified for his maiden PDC European Tour stage appearance in Kiel while still competing on the youth circuit.
quote: Winning a Tour Card at 18 and lifting my first Development Tour title shows that all the hours on the practice board are paying off.
fun_fact: Born in June 2007, Hofkens won the 2023 WDF Europe Cup Youth singles gold medal and secured his PDC Tour Card outright at Q-School while still just 18 years old.
bio: Yorick Hofkens is a teenage German professional darts prodigy who won the 2023 WDF Europe Cup Youth singles title before capturing a PDC Tour Card outright at 2026 European Q-School at age 18. He has since won a PDC Development Tour title and debuted at the UK Open.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Yorick Hofkens — Teenage German prodigy who won a PDC Tour Card at 18 and lifted his first Development Tour crown in 2026. #DartsDaily

name: Pascal Rupprecht
highlights: 2023 PDC World Youth Championship Quarter-Finalist: Reached the last eight of the prestigious youth championship while posting a 109.31 high average on the Development Tour.
Two-Time European Q-School Graduate (2023 & 2026): Earned his maiden Tour Card in 2023 and reclaimed full-time status via the 2026 European Q-School rankings.
Three-Time PDC European Tour Qualifier (2023): Qualified for the European Darts Open, European Darts Grand Prix, and International Darts Open in his rookie ProTour year.
Three-Time UK Open Competitor (2023, 2024, 2026): Competed in three editions of the televised major in Minehead.
DDV German National Ranking Champion: Captured multiple German national titles before turning full-time professional.
quote: Having lived in both Ireland and Germany gave me a unique path into the sport—winning my Tour Card back for 2026 was the top priority.
fun_fact: Born in Bielefeld, Germany, Rupprecht spent several years living in Killarney, County Kerry, Ireland—where he sharpened his game in Irish leagues—before returning to Germany and winning two PDC Tour Cards.
bio: Pascal Rupprecht is a German professional darts player and former PDC World Youth Championship quarter-finalist who first won a Tour Card in 2023. After regaining his full-time PDC status at 2026 European Q-School, he returned to the UK Open and ProTour circuit.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Pascal Rupprecht — Bielefeld's two-time Q-School graduate and former World Youth quarter-finalist back on the PDC ProTour. #DartsDaily

name: Marvin Kraft
highlights: First PDC Tour Card (2026): Secured a two-year Tour Card via the 2026 European Q-School Order of Merit in Kalkar.
2026 Poland Darts Open Qualifier: Won a Tour Card Holder Qualifier to earn his maiden PDC European Tour stage appearance.
2026 UK Open Debut: Competed in his first televised PDC major in Minehead following his Q-School graduation.
2023 PDC World Youth Championship Group Winner: Whitewashed Sam Cromwell 5–0 and pushed Josh Rock to a 5–4 deciding leg in the youth championship.
100.20 Development Tour High Average: Recorded a ton-plus average on the PDC Development Tour in Hildesheim prior to stepping up to the senior tour.
quote: Coming through European Q-School to earn a Tour Card is a huge step forward—competing week in, week out on the ProTour is the best schooling in darts.
fun_fact: Before earning his senior PDC Tour Card in 2026, Kraft turned heads at the 2023 PDC World Youth Championship by taking reigning champion Josh Rock all the way to a 5–4 deciding leg.
bio: Marvin Kraft is a German professional darts player who progressed from the PDC Development Tour to capture his first PDC Tour Card at 2026 European Q-School. In his rookie full-time season, he debuted at the UK Open and qualified for the PDC European Tour.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Marvin Kraft — Bavaria's 2026 Q-School graduate making his mark on the PDC ProTour and European Tour. #DartsDaily

name: Pero Ljubic
hometown: Golling an der Salzach / Salzburg, Austria
walk_on_music: Bonnie Tyler - I Need A Hero
highlights: First PDC Tour Card (2025): Earned a two-year Tour Card via the 2025 European Q-School Order of Merit to join Boris Krčmar as Croatia's Tour Card representatives.
European Tour Qualifier Nine-Darter (2025): Struck a nine-dart finish against Kai Gotthardt during the 2025 Hungarian Darts Trophy Tour Card Holder Qualifier.
2026 PDC World Cup of Darts Representative: Represented Croatia on the international stage in Frankfurt.
Back-to-Back UK Open Appearances (2025 & 2026): Competed in consecutive televised UK Open campaigns in Minehead.
Two-Time East Europe European Tour Qualifier (2019 & 2020): Qualified twice for the European Darts Grand Prix in Germany earlier in his career.
quote: Representing Croatia at the World Cup of Darts and holding a PDC Tour Card are proud moments for Croatian darts.
fun_fact: Ljubić fired a nine-dart finish—finishing on T20–T19–D12—against Kai Gotthardt during a 2025 European Tour qualifier in Hildesheim and represented Croatia at the 2026 PDC World Cup of Darts.
bio: Pero Ljubić is a Croatian professional darts player who secured his maiden PDC Tour Card at 2025 European Q-School. He has since struck a nine-dart finish in a European Tour qualifier, competed in two UK Opens, and represented Croatia at the 2026 PDC World Cup of Darts.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Pero Ljubić — The Croatian Knight. World Cup representative and nine-dart hero flying the flag for Croatia on the PDC Tour. #DartsDaily

name: Filip Bereza
highlights: Undefeated Q-School Debut Champion (2026): Went completely unbeaten across both Stage 1 and Stage 2 on his first-ever Q-School appearance in January 2026, winning Day 1 of the Final Stage to clinch a Tour Card.
2026 UK Open Debut: Made his first televised PDC major appearance in Minehead during his rookie campaign on the ProTour.
2025 World Masters Competitor: Competed on the WDF/PDC international stage prior to his Q-School fairy tale.
Signature Loxley Equipment Launch (2026): Released his signature 23g 95% tungsten barrels shortly after turning full-time professional.
Poland's Newest ProTour Contender: Joined Krzysztof Ratajski, Sebastian Białecki, and Tytus Kanik among Poland's full-time PDC Tour Card holders.
quote: Going undefeated on my Q-School debut to win a Tour Card felt like a dream—now I'm focused on building consistency every week on the ProTour.
fun_fact: In January 2026, Bereza pulled off one of Q-School's rarest feats by going completely undefeated through both the First Stage and Day 1 of the Final Stage on his debut appearance to capture a two-year PDC Tour Card.
bio: Filip Bereza is a Polish professional darts player who stunned the sport in January 2026 by going undefeated on his Q-School debut to capture a two-year PDC Tour Card. He made his televised major debut at the 2026 UK Open and joined Poland's growing contingent on the ProTour.
share_text: Darts Daily Player of the Day: Filip Bereza — The Breeze. Warsaw's undefeated Q-School debut sensation bringing fresh Polish firepower to the PDC Tour. #DartsDaily

name: Matthias Ehlers
walk_on_music: Die Toten Hosen - Tage wie diese
highlights: Outright European Q-School Day 3 Winner (2026): Captured the Day 3 final at 2026 European Q-School in Kalkar to earn his maiden two-year PDC Tour Card.
Two-Time 2024 European Tour Host Nation Qualifier: Qualified for both the 2024 German Darts Grand Prix in Munich and the 2024 German Darts Championship in Hildesheim.
101.55 Q-School High Average: Posted a 101.55 three-dart average against Ricky de Vos on the European Q-School stage.
PDC Europe Next Gen & Super League Contender: Built his competitive pedigree across German national and PDC Europe secondary events before turning full-time professional.
Full-Time 2026 ProTour Debutant: Competed across the 2026 Players Championship circuit, recording averages over 91 against top-32 seeds like Martin Schindler.
quote: After qualifying for European Tour events in front of home crowds in 2024, winning my Tour Card outright at Q-School was the next big goal.
fun_fact: Before winning his PDC Tour Card outright on Day 3 of 2026 European Q-School, Ehlers gained valuable stage experience by coming through two Host Nation Qualifiers to play at the German Darts Grand Prix and German Darts Championship in 2024.
bio: Matthias Ehlers is a German professional darts player who qualified for two home PDC European Tour events in 2024 before winning his first PDC Tour Card outright on Day 3 of 2026 European Q-School. He has since competed full-time across the 2026 Players Championship floor.
